topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

sections.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
lecture_lines: Planar graphs have no intersecting edges.
Faces are regions bounded by Edges.
Consider the infinite exterior region as a face.
animations: Fade in a simple planar graph with 3 vertices and 3 edges (a triangle) centered at C1. Color: #FFFFFF.
Label vertices V=3, edges E=3, faces F=1 near the triangle. Color: #FFD700.
Highlight edges to show they don't cross in a plane. Color: #00FF00.
Fade in a second graph, K3,3, which has intersecting edges at C3. Color: #FF4500.
Highlight the intersection point in K3,3 to demonstrate non-planarity. Color: #FF0000.

sections.title: The Golden Rule: Euler's Characteristic Formula
lecture_lines: Euler's formula defines a fundamental invariant.
Sum Vertices, subtract Edges, add Faces.
For connected graphs, this equals two.
It holds regardless of graph complexity.
The value two always remains constant.
animations: Display formula: V - E + F = 2 in center. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate substituting V=3, E=3, F=2 for the triangle graph below formula. Color: #00FFFF.
Display a complex graph (e.g., a square with one diagonal) and calculate V=4, E=6, F=4. Color: #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Concept of the Dual Graph
lecture_lines: Construct dual graphs by placing points.
Place a point in every face.
Connect points if faces share edges.
animations: Display a primal planar graph in #FFFFFF and place a new vertex point in each face. Color: #FFD700.
Draw dual edges between these new vertices if primal faces share a boundary edge. Color: #00FF00.
Fade out the primal graph, highlighting only the dual graph. Color: #FFD700.

sections.title: The Relationship Between Primal and Dual
lecture_lines: Primal Vertices map to Dual Faces.
Primal Edges map to Dual Edges.
Primal Faces map to Dual Vertices.
animations: Display Primal Graph (Left, D3) and Dual Graph (Right, D4) side-by-side. Colors: #FFFFFF, #FFD700.
Highlight a Primal Vertex degree (circle) mapping to a Dual Face degree (circle). Color: #00FFFF.
Flash both graphs to emphasize the dual structural relationship. Color: #FFD700.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Crucial for printed circuit board design.
Useful for coloring maps and networks.
animations: Show a simplified printed circuit board schematic diagram. Color: #FFFFFF.
Superimpose the dual graph (in dashed lines) over the circuit components. Color: #FFD700.
Label nodes in the dual graph as network components to demonstrate utility. Color: #00FF00.
